Hi Daniel — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a concise evidence packet that addresses items 1–4 and proposing an operational approach for a short-term access carve-out. Highlights below; full detail is in the PDF and CSV attached.

- SLOs: We define uptime at the service ingress level. Dedicated capacity default SLO = 99.95% monthly availability (measured as successful request completion / total attempts, excluding scheduled maintenance windows and customer-initiated traffic limits). Latency SLOs: p95 <= 120ms, p99 <= 450ms for text-generation requests with payloads <= 512 tokens; note that long-context or tool-calling flows have adjusted thresholds included in the packet. Measurement uses synthetic probes + sampled production traffic with a bias correction to account for sampling.
- Monitoring telemetry: We expose request_count, request_success, request_latency_ms (histogram buckets), model_variant, region, and customer_id tags. Retention: raw high-cardinality metrics retained for 30 days, aggregated rollups (1h bins) for 365 days. Sampling: for tenants above a token/sec threshold we apply deterministic sampling (1/N) and attach a sampling_factor tag so rates can be reconstructed.
- Alerting: Critical incidents triggered on error_rate > 0.5% for 5m or sustained p99 latency > 1s for 10m. Warnings issued for transient spikes; incidents route to our infra on-call with a documented escalation playbook included.
- Customer access: we can provide read-only Grafana dashboard invites (templated per-customer view) + CSV exports of queried time ranges. Exports include sampling_factor so you can compute extrapolated counts.

Temporary carve-out: we support a 72-hour read-only dashboard invitation for procurement/security review by request. Authorization requires: (1) procurement email/named approver, (2) signed NDA if required by the customer's policy, and (3) a start/end time. Access is audited; we provide an export of access logs after the window closes.

I've attached: redwood_slo-evidence_v1.pdf (SLO definitions + methodology), telemetry-schema-2026.csv (metric names & tags), and a Grafana invite stub (we'll send a real .ics/URL once you confirm the approver list).

Hi team — answers below, keeping language procurement-friendly so we can paste into the packet.

1) Sampling reconstruction: We attach a sampling_factor tag at the earliest sampling point (typically ingress). To compute estimated total events you multiply observed_count * sampling_factor. If a request passes multiple sampled stages we track the highest-resolution sampling_factor and document the join semantics in the CSV (see telemetry-schema-2026.csv attached). Example: if ingress sampling_factor=10 and runtime sampling not applied, observed 1,234 events -> estimated 12,340 events. We include the formula and a worked example in the PDF.

2) Isolation/redaction: read-only Grafana views never surface raw request payloads. For procurement validation we will: (a) disable any panel that would expose request_id -> raw payload joins, (b) mask customer_id with a reversible token inside our audit-only dataset if needed, and (c) only grant access to a pre-approved email list. No downstream storage of payload data is exposed through Grafana exports.

Operational notes on carve-out: Access is timeboxed to the requested window; we generate an access log and a short report showing which dashboards/panels were viewed. For exceptional evidence that requires sample traces we can provide redacted traces under a controlled NDA process.

Let me know if you want the security team to add a one-paragraph assurance note about not sharing payloads — I can draft it.

-Vivek
